    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.RingTheory.Idempotents.Corner.Basic, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Corners cut out by two idempotents #

    Let A be a nonunital algebra over a semiring k: a nonunital semiring with a k-module structure whose scalar multiplication commutes with multiplication on either side. This file defines the corner eAf as the range of Mathlib's LinearMap.mulLeftRight k (e, f), the linear map x ↦ e * x * f. When e and f are idempotent, membership is equivalent to the fixed-point equation e * x * f = x.

    The second part concerns Mathlib's corner ring IsIdempotentElem.Corner of an idempotent e, the ring eAe with unit e. Mathlib gives it a semiring structure even when A has no unit, and a ring structure when A is a nonunital ring. The corner inherits the compatible scalar action and module structure of A. Over a commutative semiring R, this makes it an R-algebra, with algebraMap R eAe r = r • e. When A is unital, this is the structure under which eAe can be compared with A as R-algebras, for instance through Mathlib's MoritaEquivalence.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.cornerSubmodule: the corner eAf, as a k-submodule of A.
    • IsIdempotentElem.Corner.instAlgebra: the corner eAe of an idempotent of a nonunital R-algebra is a unital R-algebra.
    • IsIdempotentElem.cornerLinearEquivCornerSubmodule: the corner ring eAe, as an R-module, agrees with the corner submodule LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.cornerSubmodule R e e.
    • IsIdempotentElem.cornerMap: a homomorphism of nonunital semirings restricts to a unital homomorphism of corners; a surjective homomorphism remains surjective on corners.
    • IsIdempotentElem.cornerEquiv: a ring equivalence restricts to an equivalence of corners.
    • IsIdempotentElem.cornerPiEquiv: the corner of an idempotent in a product of rings is the product of the corners of its components.
    • IsIdempotentElem.isNoetherian_corner: the corner of a Noetherian algebra is Noetherian, so the corner of a finite-dimensional algebra is finite-dimensional.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.mem_cornerSubmodule_iff: the fixed-point characterization of an idempotent corner.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.mem_span_singleton_of_mem_cornerSubmodule: the corner eAf lies in the left ideal Af without idempotency assumptions.
    • IsIdempotentElem.mul_corner_val and IsIdempotentElem.corner_val_mul: an element of the corner ring eAe is fixed by e on both sides.
    • Pi.isIdempotentElem_iff: an element of a product is idempotent exactly when each component is.

    References #

    See I. Assem, D. Simson, A. Skowroński, Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras, Vol. 1, Section I.4.
